parts.description: A cylindrical light grey concrete pot filled with artificial green and pink succulent plants surrounded by small pebbles.
parts.reasoning: The dominant structural and contact material for this object is the cylindrical base, which appears to be made of unglazed concrete or a similar heavy, porous ceramic. Consequently, the root-level physics properties (density, friction, restitution) are based on concrete. A pot of this apparent size (approx. 15-20 cm diameter) filled with dirt/pebbles and plants is relatively heavy, estimated at 1.5 kg. Concrete has high friction and low restitution (bounciness). For collision geometry, 'convex_decomposition' is highly recommended; a simple bounding cylinder or convex hull would incorrectly encompass the empty space between the plant leaves, whereas a decomposition will create a stable cylindrical base while roughly approximating the bumpy top surface of the succulents, allowing for realistic interaction if objects fall on it.
